hyperedges.label: Phase 2 fixtures exercising the connector router
RCON apply batch-size limits and spec splitting
Solar farm to assembly electric network
Electric pole coverage and placement rules learned live

nodes.label: belt_segment function
nodes.rationale: Phase 2 fixture: the simplest possible function - a straight run of `length` belt tiles with in/out ports at each end - deliberately kept free of furnace-footprint geometry so it exercises connect.ts's router in isolation.

nodes.label: furnace_row function
nodes.rationale: A row of `count` electric-furnaces, each fed by an inserter from a shared vertical input belt and unloaded by an inserter onto a shared vertical output belt. Works for any ore because furnaces auto-detect their recipe from input material.

nodes.label: gear_assembler function
nodes.rationale: One assembling-machine-3 crafting iron-gear-wheel from a dedicated iron-plate input onto an output belt. Unlike a furnace, assembling machines do support set_recipe - verified, since the failure ('Entity is not assembling-machine') is furnace-specific.

nodes.label: science_assembler function
nodes.rationale: One assembling-machine-3 crafting automation-science-pack, needing two dedicated inputs (copper-plate from the west, iron-gear-wheel from the north), so it carries two separate belt+inserter pairs feeding the same machine.

nodes.label: single_pole function
nodes.rationale: One medium-electric-pole used to relay the grid between distant functions. It declares no ports at all, because power connects wirelessly via supply_radius/wire_reach rather than through the connector router.

nodes.label: smelting_column function
nodes.rationale: Phase 2 fixture with parameterized furnace_count/furnace_type/recipe. It has no inserters, so it would not actually smelt anything if run for real - the belt lane just runs past the furnaces. It exists to exercise the format mechanism (params, repeat, ports, the router), not as a working blueprint.

nodes.label: solar_row function
nodes.rationale: A row of `count` solar panels plus enough medium-electric-poles to cover all of them; declares no ports since power is wireless. Pole count is fixed at 3 for count=5 rather than param-scaled because the expression language has no integer division or modulo yet.

nodes.label: test_smelter function
nodes.rationale: Phase 4 fixture, deliberately outside the port/connection system (inserters are not a port kind): a small ad hoc rig - burner-inserter plus stone-furnace - whose only job is to produce a real, measurable 'iron-plate produced' stat for testing apply --smoke-check against factorio-broadcast's /api/stats. Its burner needs fuel, topped up once via RCON for the test.

nodes.label: Auto-fill straight/L connector router
nodes.rationale: Given two already-laid-out absolute ports, fills the gap with belt/pipe entities or emits a wire op. A full pathfinding autorouter is explicitly out of scope for v1 - constraining the geometry to straight-or-single-bend keeps routing decidable and the failure mode explicit.

nodes.label: Compiler pipeline
nodes.rationale: parse -> resolveFunctions -> layout (absolute coords + rotation, bbox-overlap check) -> connect -> ir (flatten to IREntity[] with deterministic localId) -> state.diff -> planBuilder. Deterministic localIds are what let the state diff match entities across runs.

nodes.label: Composition spec (*.spec.yaml)
nodes.rationale: Imports function definitions, places instances on a grid with params, declares the RCON server target, and wires named ports between instances.

nodes.label: Function definition (*.function.yaml)
nodes.rationale: A fixed-footprint, reusable block of entities with named ports on its perimeter, parameterized so one definition serves many instances.

nodes.label: L-bend connector case
nodes.rationale: Valid when the two port directions are perpendicular and the one compatible corner gives two unobstructed legs. No corner prototype is needed because Factorio auto-curves belts from neighbor direction; pipes reuse the same two-leg geometry without a directionality constraint.

nodes.label: params / repeat / ${expr} templating
nodes.rationale: Typed params with defaults, a repeat count with an implicit index i, and ${...} expressions in sizes, positions and port offsets are what make one function definition reusable across instances; resolved by resolveFunctions before layout.

nodes.label: Named port
nodes.rationale: Fields are side (validated against offset at load time), offset (function-local tiles), direction, kind (belt|pipe|wire) and item/fluid/signal. Direction always means 'material moves this way at that exact tile', so the connector router never has to flip anything and only checks colinearity.

nodes.label: Resource-backed instance
nodes.rationale: An instance with a resource and patch_id instead of a hand-authored function; the function is synthesized either by the drill placer (real_drills) or as an infinity-chest/pipe stub for testing. Both modes expose the same downstream ports so a spec can swap resource_mode once the placer is trusted without rewiring.

nodes.label: state.diff against factoriollm.state.json
nodes.rationale: Diffing the flattened IR against persisted state is what makes apply idempotent and produces both the op list and the human-readable diff.

nodes.label: Straight connector case
nodes.rationale: Valid only when both port directions are equal and axis-aligned with the A->B vector and every intermediate tile is unobstructed.

nodes.label: UNROUTABLE_CONNECTION compile error
nodes.rationale: Anything the router cannot handle is a hard compile error collected across the whole spec rather than fail-fast, so an author sees every unroutable connection in one pass; the message names both ports, their coordinates and facings, and suggests repositioning or an intermediate connection.

nodes.label: Wire connector case
nodes.rationale: No belt/pipe geometry at all - only a max_reach distance check, emitted as a direct LuaWireConnector:connect_to op with no intermediate entities.

nodes.label: 60 SPM self-sustained vanilla build
nodes.rationale: 80 solar panels power 6 real ore-to-plate electric-furnace smelters plus 1 gear and 4 science assembling-machine-3. The two halves are not wired end to end because a real Factorio production-bus problem (not a factoriollm one) got in the way, so the assemblers are fed by dedicated infinity-chest stubs.

nodes.label: factorio-broadcast sibling project
nodes.rationale: Provides the shared WSL2 headless dev server and its /api/stats endpoint; factoriollm deliberately does not stand up its own server and wraps the sibling's dev.sh for lifecycle.

nodes.label: Companion Lua mod
nodes.rationale: Applies a plan via the Factorio API; decodes the plan JSON string with helpers.json_to_table before factoriollm.apply sees it.

nodes.label: packages/cli factoriollm binary
nodes.rationale: Exposes ping / validate / plan / apply / destroy. Must run under WSL's node rather than Windows' because it talks to a server that only exists inside WSL.

nodes.label: packages/compiler
nodes.rationale: Holds the parse -> layout -> ir -> state (diff) -> planBuilder pipeline; compiled with tsc to plain JS so it runs under WSL's node even though npm install happens on the Windows side (this WSL2 instance has no outbound network).

nodes.label: scripts/dev.sh wrapper
nodes.rationale: Wraps factorio-broadcast's dev.sh for server lifecycle (mod / start / ping) instead of duplicating server management.

nodes.label: apply --smoke-check
nodes.rationale: Verifies a build by reading real production stats rather than trusting the apply result; used to confirm exact rates (not just nonzero) after apply.

nodes.label: factoriollm
nodes.rationale: An LLM-authorable declarative YAML format for Factorio factories deployed to a headless server. Entities are created directly via the Lua API with no player, inventory or character, so builds are reproducible and machine-authorable rather than depending on in-game hand placement.

nodes.label: v1 four-way direction restriction
nodes.rationale: Directions are restricted to N/E/S/W in v1 because only straight and L-bend routing is in scope; diagonal or arbitrary angles would require a real autorouter.

nodes.label: v1 update policy: in-place vs destroy+recreate
nodes.norm_label: v1 update policy: in-place vs destroy+recreate
nodes.rationale: Only recipe and filter fields (set_recipe, set_filter) update in place; any position/direction/name change is destroy+recreate, because those are the only mutations the Factorio API can apply safely without reasoning about footprint moves.

nodes.label: Electric-only furnace choice
nodes.rationale: electric-furnace was chosen over stone-furnace to avoid coal-fuel logistics entirely - the whole project's power design is electric-only, so no fuel belts or refuelling inserters ever have to be modeled.

nodes.label: in-port y:1 alignment to the belt tile
nodes.norm_label: in-port y:1 alignment to the belt tile
nodes.rationale: The in port sits at y:1, not y:0, because the first row's actual belt tile is aligned to the furnace's 3-tall center row. Getting it wrong left a 1-tile gap the connector never filled, confirmed live as ore piling up on the connector's last tile while the function's own belt stayed empty.

nodes.label: 4-tile row spacing for pole gap
nodes.rationale: Rows are spaced 4 apart although a furnace is only 3 tall, to leave a 1-tile gap for a power pole. Placing the pole inside the furnace's own footprint was tried first and silently failed the placement guard, the same way the solar farm's pole mistake did.

nodes.label: Pole placement vs connector L-bend collision
nodes.norm_label: pole placement vs connector l-bend collision
nodes.rationale: No pole may sit on local column x=0 at y<3, because that is exactly where an incoming connector's L-bend corner and leg land whenever the source chest shares the instance's y - which every example here does. Confirmed live as a real placement collision twice.

nodes.label: Three poles for supply-radius coverage
nodes.rationale: Three medium-electric-poles, not one: across a 9x6 function a single pole's supply_radius of 3.5 cannot reach both the north inserter and the east output inserter from any corner. Confirmed live as two of three inserters reporting no_power while the third, nearer the pole, worked.

nodes.label: Infinity-chest void sink
nodes.rationale: An inserter moves output off the belt into an infinity-chest filtered at-most 0, deleting anything beyond that. Without it, the output belt and then the assembler back up to full_output within ~30 seconds when nothing is downstream, which silently stops production rather than erroring - confirmed live as the measured rate collapsing from 60/min to 8/min. Specifically a trap for throughput tests.

nodes.label: supply_radius vs wire_reach pole spacing
nodes.rationale: One end-pole is not enough: a medium-electric-pole's supply_radius is only 3.5 tiles, so a panel more than ~7 tiles from the nearest pole reports not_plugged_in_electric_network (confirmed on a real placed panel) even though wire_reach of 9 would happily link the poles to each other. Poles ~6 tiles apart keep every panel inside someone's supply radius. Poles go at y=3, just south of the 3-tall panel row, not inside it.

nodes.label: Inserter direction means pickup side
nodes.rationale: Verified live: an inserter's direction is its PICKUP side and the drop is the opposite tile - backwards from the naive 'direction = drop side' assumption. 'west' picks up from the west tile and drops on the east one.

nodes.label: Live-testing discipline over type checking
nodes.rationale: Every phase is verified against a live server rather than only type-checked, because the bugs that mattered were all false assumptions about the Factorio API that a type checker cannot see: nonexistent helpers.read_file, double-sent RCON, missing footprint-aware center-offset math, unresolved ${expr} templates in port offsets, set_recipe failing on furnaces, inserter direction meaning pickup side, and the stats API nesting production by time window rather than flat.

nodes.label: Terraform-style plan/apply/destroy lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Infrastructure-as-code semantics were chosen deliberately: a spec is written, `plan` shows the diff, `apply` pushes it, state is tracked so re-applying is idempotent, and `destroy` tears it down. Idempotence is what makes an LLM-authored spec safe to re-run.

nodes.label: 50,000 character plan size guard
nodes.rationale: Delivery was tested to 100,000 characters in one command with no issue, but the CLI refuses anything over 50,000 rather than silently failing, because chunked delivery for larger plans is not implemented yet.

nodes.label: RCON-argument plan delivery
nodes.rationale: Factorio's Lua API can write to script-output/ but cannot read arbitrary files back (helpers.read_file does not exist - verified live, not assumed; the original plan-delivery design wrongly assumed it did). So the plan JSON travels as the RCON command's own argument, passed as a Lua string literal because JSON and Lua table-literal syntax are incompatible. Replies are not constrained the same way, so results come back as remote.call's return value.

nodes.label: RCON single-send correctness
nodes.rationale: Blindly double-sending every RCON command (a pattern borrowed from factorio-broadcast's scripts/rcon.js) double-executes side-effecting Lua - one create_entity became two entities - while 'take the last reply' hid it for idempotent output, which is why the ping test never caught it. The client sends once and only resends on an actual 'please repeat' prompt.

nodes.label: set_recipe unsupported on furnaces
nodes.rationale: Only assembling-machines support set_recipe; furnaces infer their recipe from their input material, so a recipe field on a furnace entity cannot be applied the same way.

nodes.label: Unimplemented wires and rotated instances
nodes.rationale: Wire connections and rotated instances (only direction: north works today) are the two things docs/FORMAT.md describes that are not implemented yet - a known documented/implemented gap.

nodes.label: infinity_chest resource mode
nodes.community_name: one assembler group per apply call
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 fixture: a resource-backed instance is stood up as a single infinity-chest stub instead of real mining infrastructure so the apply/plan round trip can be tested with no hand-authored function and no connections. apply creates exactly one infinity-chest at the declared position; running plan immediately after must show no diff, which is the idempotency check the stub exists to prove.

nodes.label: real_drills resource mode
nodes.community_name: one assembler group per apply call
nodes.rationale: Phase 3 fixture: instead of faking supply with an infinity chest, a live-scanned ore patch is greedily covered with electric-mining-drills over a declared bounding_box. The bounding_box was not hand-estimated - it came straight from `factoriollm scan-resources` output and was cross-checked against a direct RCON find_entities_filtered count (325 tiles, 718477 amount, exact match) before being pasted into the spec, so the fixture is anchored to real map data.

nodes.label: direct-adjacency placement (no connections block)
nodes.community_name: one assembler group per apply call
nodes.rationale: The chest and the inserter are placed touching each other directly rather than routed through connect.ts, because inserters are not a belt/pipe/wire port kind and therefore have no representation in the connections model. The spec deliberately omits a `connections:` block so the smoke check exercises placement and item flow without exercising the router.

nodes.label: straight belt route (axis-aligned gap fill)
nodes.community_name: one assembler group per apply call
nodes.rationale: Phase 2 happy-path fixture for connect.ts: the two belt_segment instances are deliberately placed with a real 3-tile gap (b1 spans y=10..13 with b1.out at absolute (10,13) facing south; b2 spans y=17..20 with b2.in at absolute (10,17) facing south) so both ports share the x axis and face the same direction. That satisfies the straight-run case, which requires axis alignment, and leaves an actual gap for the router to fill rather than letting the belts touch.

nodes.label: UNROUTABLE_CONNECTION hard-fail case
nodes.community_name: one assembler group per apply call
nodes.rationale: Phase 2 negative fixture. smelt1.out and smelt2.in both face south (same direction, not perpendicular) but are offset diagonally, so neither router case applies: the straight case needs axis alignment and the L-bend case needs perpendicular port directions. `factoriollm validate` must reject this with UNROUTABLE_CONNECTION during static validation and never touch RCON, proving routing errors are caught before any live mutation.

nodes.label: one assembler group per apply call
nodes.community_name: one assembler group per apply call
nodes.norm_label: one assembler group per apply call
nodes.rationale: Each science_assembler group lives in its own spec file because apply() doing too much work in a single RCON round trip was silently dropping the reply past roughly 50 entities. One assembler group plus its two feed chests is the empirically reliable unit size for a single apply, so the 60 SPM science stage is split one-group-per-file rather than expressed as one spec.

nodes.label: apply() per-invocation work limit (empty RCON reply)
nodes.community_name: one assembler group per apply call
nodes.norm_label: apply() per-invocation work limit (empty rcon reply)
nodes.rationale: A second failure mode distinct from the 50,000-char command-length check: a 57-entity batch (gear_demo + science1 + science2) came back with an empty RCON reply even though roughly 52 of the 57 entities were actually created, confirmed live. The cause is apply() doing too much work inside one Lua invocation, not command length, so the fix was splitting to one assembler group per apply call as the reliable unit size. This file is part 2a of the assembly stage and carries only gear_demo.

nodes.label: one dedicated chest per furnace
nodes.community_name: one assembler group per apply call
nodes.rationale: Each furnace gets its own infinity chest rather than sharing one belt across several, because it was verified live that a single inserter on a shared belt drains 100% of supply before it can reach a second consumer (see drillPlacer.ts). Every furnace_row here uses count:1, so the layout is really four separate iron smelters and two separate copper smelters, each self-contained.

nodes.label: frozen daytime=0 solar convention
nodes.community_name: one assembler group per apply call
nodes.rationale: The test map uses surf.daytime=0 with surf.freeze_daytime=true, where 0 is full daylight on this server. 0.5 was initially assumed to be noon but turned out to be when panels report no_power. Freezing at 0 makes solar output constant so the build needs no accumulators. This is a test-setup step, deliberately not part of the spec format.

nodes.label: 50,000-char single-RCON-command safety limit
nodes.community_name: one assembler group per apply call
nodes.rationale: One spec covering the whole factory compiles to a plan JSON above the 50,000-char single-RCON-command safety limit (326 entities is roughly 54,000 chars), and chunked delivery is not implemented yet (see packages/cli/src/deploy/trigger.ts). The 60 SPM build is therefore split into halves that each apply independently with their own state file.

nodes.label: single_pole relay spine (wire_reach 9)
nodes.community_name: one assembler group per apply call
nodes.rationale: Three relay columns stitch the solar farm into one electric network reaching east. Solar rows' own poles sit at absolute x=13.5, and with wire_reach 9 relays at x=20 (6.5 from the spine) spaced 8 apart vertically link the farm. The second column at x=37 is offset to y=3/15/27 rather than 0/15/30 because furnace poles sit at absolute y=3,9,15,21,27,33; relay10 at y=15 measured exactly 9.0 and connected, while relay9/11 at un-aligned y measured 9.49 to the nearest furnace pole, just over the limit, and came up live as isolated single-pole networks. A third column at x=43 was needed because x=37 is 13 tiles from the assembly stage's poles at x=50, which exceeds wire_reach and was confirmed live as an isolated network; x=43 sits within reach of both.
